title: Gov311 entry
description: Front matter for one Markdown entry. The entry type comes from its folder: services, contacts, codes, or help.

sources.description: Official pages where a reader can confirm the facts in this entry.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences. Search results show this text.

keywords.description: Words people actually use when they ask about this, including informal ones.

last_verified.description: Date the named person or tool last checked the guide against its sources, or researched it if still a draft.

verified_by.description: GitHub username of the person or name of the tool that performed the latest check or draft research.

trust.description: draft: the source check is incomplete. source-checked: the named person or tool checked the guide's material claims against official sources. community: a human contributor checked it. verified: a second person independently confirmed it. official: a government employee submitted or confirmed it.

human_review.description: Unresolved facts a person needs to check. Record what is missing or which official sources disagree.

department.description: Path of the contact entry for the office that handles this, relative to the jurisdiction folder. Example: contacts/codes-department

timeline.description: How long it usually takes, as the agency states it.

deadline.description: A filing deadline, if one applies.

official_text.description: Where the authoritative text of the law or code is published. Required for entries in codes/.

access.description: open: anyone and any tool can read it. captcha: the site makes visitors prove they are a person. blocks-automated-tools: the site turns away AI tools and scripts without showing a challenge. login: needs a free account. paywall: costs money.

how_to_find.description: How to get from this link to the right section.

covers.description: The questions this law or code answers, as short topics. Do not state the answers.

unofficial_copies.description: Open copies of this law from an established legal publisher, a university, or a public-interest archive. They let an AI tool read the text when the official site blocks it. They carry no legal weight and can be out of date.

guides.description: Plain-language explanations of this law published by a government or a legal aid organization.
